prompt:
Implement satisfies(version, range_str) and max_satisfying(versions, range_str) in src/semver/range.py. Ranges follow node-semver (the npm semver package) in its default mode: not loose, prereleases not included by default.
- Comparators <, <=, >, >=, = (or no operator) separated by spaces must all hold; comparator sets separated by || are alternatives.
- Hyphen ranges (A - B), X-ranges (x, X, * or missing parts), tilde (~, ~>) and caret (^) ranges mean exactly what they mean in node-semver.
- A version with a prerelease tag satisfies a comparator set only if some comparator in that set has a prerelease tag on the same major.minor.patch.
- Build metadata is ignored.
An invalid range or version raises ValueError. max_satisfying returns the highest of the given version strings (as given) that satisfies the range, or None; strings that are not valid versions are skipped.
One test in tests/ fails; fix the bug behind it.
Add tests for the new behaviour. Run all tests with: PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .
notes: calibration candidate (4b), stdlib only, built by lab/tasks/build_tasks.py; traps: numeric prerelease identifiers (public); ^0.x / ^0.0.x; >1.2 means >=1.3.0, <=1.2 means <1.3.0; hyphen with partial upper bound; prerelease rule needs same major.minor.patch; * does not match prereleases; <1.2.3 does not match 1.2.3-beta; || sets evaluated separately for the prerelease rule
